lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals and Fueling My Day
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: naming a signal kindly

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 4 — body signals, rest, and food variety
objective: Learners sort four example sentences about body signals into neutral-naming and self-critical groups, then rewrite each self-critical sentence using the calm starter phrase 'My body is telling me,' so they build a habit of describing a signal factually instead of judging themselves for having it.
scenario: The learner reads four printed example sentences a kid might say about a body signal, some worded kindly and some worded with frustration or shame, sorts all four into two groups, and rewrites every self-critical sentence into a neutral version using the same naming starter each time.
materials: the four example sentences provided in this lesson

tasks.directions: Read all four example sentences quietly before sorting anything.

prompts.text: Of the four sentences, which one would feel kindest to hear someone say about themselves, and what specific word made it feel kind?

tasks.directions: Sort the four sentences into two groups, neutral naming and self-critical, then rewrite each self-critical sentence using the starter 'My body is telling me.'

prompts.text: I sorted all four sentences into 'neutral naming' or 'self-critical' before rewriting any of them.
I rewrote each self-critical sentence starting with the exact phrase 'My body is telling me.'
I kept the same signal (hunger, thirst, tiredness, or another signal) in my rewrite instead of changing it to a different signal.
I read my rewritten sentences out loud to check that they sound calm, not judgmental.

tasks.directions: Without looking at the four example sentences, apply the same starter phrase to a signal you have felt today.

prompts.text: Write one neutral naming sentence about a signal you have felt today, using the starter 'My body is telling me.'

tasks.directions: Think of one sentence you have heard someone say about a body signal that sounded unkind or impatient, from a book, a show, or somewhere you have been.

prompts.text: Write the unkind sentence you thought of, then write a kinder, neutral version of that same sentence using today's starter phrase.

remediation: If a learner rewrites a self-critical sentence by erasing the signal entirely, such as changing it to 'I'm fine,' reteach with a two-column matching drill that requires the specific signal word to appear in every rewrite before it counts as complete.
extension: Have the learner write three example naming sentences as if teaching the starter phrase to a favorite character from a book or show, using a different signal in each sentence.
